title: Connexions de Gauss-Manin et équations de Picard-Fuchs. Opération de Cartier : copies de tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), tiré à part (1981), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting, from this and the neighbouring pages: X/S is a smooth relative curve over a base S of characteristic 0, with relative 1-form ω. L = Σ_i D_i ∇^i is a Picard-Fuchs operator for the class of ω. Read in the usual way, it satisfies an exact relation Σ_i D_i ∇^i ω = dφ, with φ a function on X; this is presumably formula (10). For two sections a, b of X→S, μ(a,b) := L(∫_{a(s)}^{b(s)} ω_s), the Picard-Fuchs operator applied to the abelian integral between the two sections. Because L kills every period, μ(a,b) is a well-defined function on S; ω_{i,s} is read as the i-th Gauss-Manin derivative of ω. This is the Manin homomorphism, or inhomogeneous Picard-Fuchs equation, from Manin's proof of function-field Mordell.

The previous page asks for μ 'par voie algébrique, sans calcul d'intégrales'. Since μ is local on S, one may assume an integrable connection on X/S, i.e. a local trivialisation. If a and b are horizontal, the endpoints do not move, so L can be passed under the integral: μ(a,b) = ∫_a^b dφ = φ(b) − φ(a) (formula 14).

This page treats general sections. Take the horizontal sections a_0, b_0 through a(s_0), b(s_0). By Chasles additivity of the path integral, μ(a,b) = μ(a_0,b_0) + μ(b_0,b) − μ(a_0,a). Hence
 μ(a,b)(s_0) = [φ(b(s_0)) − φ(a(s_0))] + (Σ_i D_i ∂^i_s ∫_{b_0(s)}^{b(s)} ω_s − Σ_i D_i ∂^i_s ∫_{a_0(s)}^{a(s)} ω_s)|_{s=s_0}.

The correction integrals vanish at s_0, but their derivatives do not. They depend only on the finite-order jets of a, b, a_0, b_0 at s_0 ('c'est une histoire purement locale').

The struck-out passage starts to make these terms algebraic. The connection lets one regard ω as a form on X, so a^*(ω) becomes a 1-form on S. If the lift of ω is closed, a^*(ω) is closed because a^* commutes with d. The derivatives of ∫_{a_0}^{a} ω would then come from a^*ω − a_0^*ω and its derivatives. The margin note 'donner une formule....!' shows the explicit jet formula was not obtained on this page.
errors: φ(b_0) − φ(a_0) = μ(a_0,b_0) holds only for the φ attached to the chosen local connection/lift. φ and the horizontal sections both depend on that choice, and the correction terms compensate; the page does not make this dependence explicit.

The ∫_{b_0(s)}^{b(s)} terms involve path integrals over small paths near b(s_0). The 'purely algebraic' expression in jets, with no integrals, is only begun and then crossed out, so the computation is incomplete.

ideas.what: Picard-Fuchs operator applied to the abelian integral between two sections gives an algebraic function μ(a,b) (inhomogeneous Picard-Fuchs equation)
ideas.modern_name: Manin homomorphism / Manin map (theorem of the kernel)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Yu. Manin (1963); later Coleman (1990), Chai, Buium, Bertrand
ideas.where_published: Not known in published Grothendieck texts; possibly in the 1972-81 Gauss-Manin/Picard-Fuchs typescript of this dossier

ideas.what: For horizontal sections relative to a local integrable connection, μ(a,b) = φ(b) − φ(a), with Σ D_i ∇^i ω = dφ
ideas.modern_name: algebraic computation of the Manin map via an exact Picard-Fuchs relation
ideas.usually_credited_to: Manin; made rigorous in Coleman's 1990 paper

ideas.what: Reduction of the general case to horizontal sections plus a local jet-dependent correction (pull-backs a^*ω as closed 1-forms on S)
ideas.modern_name: Manin map as a differential-algebraic (order-bounded) operator on sections; jet description

missed.claim: Grothendieck sets out to give an explicit integral-free formula for the Manin map μ(a,b) for non-horizontal sections, in terms of jets of the sections and pull-backs a^*ω. He leaves it unfinished, with the marginal note 'donner une formule....!'.
missed.quote: Il faut calculer les deux termes ... c'est une histoire purement locale ... donner une formule....!
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is mainly of historical interest. It documents Grothendieck working on an algebraic treatment of Manin's map, with rigour issues (cf. Coleman's 1990 gap correction), well before the later literature. The mathematics itself was later settled by Coleman, Chai and Buium.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a careful but routine local computation of the Manin map/inhomogeneous Picard-Fuchs term, and it is left unfinished. Its interest is mainly historical: it shows Grothendieck engaging with Manin's function-field Mordell machinery.
transcription_corrections: Read the fragmentary line as 'Il faut calculer les deux termes de droite ... c'est une histoire purement locale'.
The struck-out passage begins roughly 'Notons que si on a une connexion intégrable sur X/S' (not 'Notons que ∇ commute à X/S').
'a^*(ω) ∈ Γ(S, a^*(Ω^1_{X/S}))' line and following: the pullback of ω via a and the connection gives a 1-form a^*(ω) ∈ Γ(S, Ω^1_S).
'Cette forme est encore fermée, si ω l'était' plus an N.B. about defining a^*(ω) via a closed form on X (a lift), noting that a^* commutes with the exterior differential.
In the displayed formula the integrals are of ω_{i,s} with coefficients D_{i,s}, presumably meaning the i-th derivative in s; the bracketed first term is φ(b(s_0)) − φ(a(s_0)).
